I have farmed in Quzhou County for a long time, so I would keep my plan practical and labor-aware. My household has only 3 people and some family labor is off-farm, so I would not spread myself too thin with complicated management. Because I have well irrigation, I would stay with the wheat-maize system as the backbone on most of my land since it is familiar, stable, and fits local conditions. I would use improved or hybrid seed on the grain crops because I care about stable yield more than saving a little on seed. For wheat, I would put enough fertilizer to secure tillering and grain filling, irrigate a few key times, and keep tillage simple with rotary cultivation. For summer maize, I would use hybrid seed, give it stronger nitrogen than wheat, irrigate when the season turns dry, and control weeds and insects with a few pesticide sprays rather than many passes. For zucchini, I would keep a smaller area as a cash crop because it needs more hands and more frequent field attention; I would manage it more intensively on fertilizer, irrigation, and pest control, but I would not expand it too much because labor is limited. Overall, I would aim for steady output, manageable labor, and low risk rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
